scope: Verified PDF filter rules and locators against ISO 32000-2:2020(E), sponsored edition including Errata Collection 3: 7.4.1-7.4.5, 7.4.10, Tables 6-10 and 14; parameter/chain context 7.3.7-7.3.9 and Table 5; whitespace 7.2.3 Table 1. Verified external framing, coding tables and predictor arithmetic against RFC 1950 (May 1996) 2.1-2.3, RFC 1951 (May 1996) 3.1-3.3, PNG Second Edition (W3C Recommendation 10 November 2003) 9.1-9.4 and Table 9.1, and TIFF Revision 6.0 (3 June 1992) sections 13-14 pp.58-65. The TIFF review covers PDF LZW correspondence and Predictor 2, not TIFF containers. Image-codec clauses 7.4.6-7.4.9 are excluded. No external primary-text review in this scope remains pending. General incomplete-Huffman-tree rejection and other documented choices are policy, not normative verdicts; caps and recovery are verified only against project policy. Representational dimension limits remain explicit gaps. Output encoding additionally verified against RFC 1950 2.2/2.3, RFC 1951 3.1.1/3.2.2-3.2.7, and PNG Second Edition 5.2-5.6, 6.2, 9, 11.2.2/11.2.4/11.2.5 and 12.8. Encoding effort, block boundaries, adaptive-filter ties and byte budgets are documented project choices.

rules.rule: FlateDecode denotes the zlib/DEFLATE method defined by RFC 1950 and RFC 1951.
rules.implementation: Agrees at the PDF boundary: wrapped data decodes, automatic raw fallback is a reported repair.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: zlib level/strategy cases, explicit raw vectors and flate-raw-repair-fixed; external bitstream rules are reviewed below.

rules.rule: Flate uses Predictor=1, Colors=1, BitsPerComponent=8 and Columns=1 when parameters are absent.
rules.implementation: Agrees for representable dimensions; EarlyChange is not a Flate parameter.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: default Flate vectors and predictor grids.

rules.rule: A null-valued parameter is absent and therefore takes its default.
rules.implementation: Agrees after fixing null predictor parameters.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-null-predictor-parameters.

rules.rule: Zlib uses CM=8, CINFO=0..7 for windows 2^(CINFO+8), and a big-endian CMF/FLG pair divisible by 31; FLEVEL is advisory.
rules.implementation: Agrees: recognized wrappers validate CINFO and FCHECK, enforce the advertised window and ignore FLEVEL; automatic raw decoding is reported.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: zlib-rfc1950-cinfo{0..7}-level{0..3}, zlib-rfc1950-invalid-cinfo, window-distance256/257 and flate-invalid-bad-fcheck.

rules.rule: FDICT announces a four-byte dictionary checksum; an enclosing format without preset dictionaries must reject FDICT.
rules.implementation: Agrees: PDF defines no preset dictionaries, so FDICT produces Syntax before dictionary-dependent inflation.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: zlib-rfc1950-fdict includes the complete dictionary identifier and payload; flate-invalid-preset-dictionary also rejects a short header.

rules.rule: Adler-32 covers all inflated bytes before predictor reversal, starts its sums at 1 and 0 modulo 65521, and stores the combined checksum big-endian.
rules.implementation: Agrees: accumulated raw bytes include PNG tags and TIFF differences; a mismatch is a tagged Strict error or reported project repair.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-checksum and flate-truncated-checksum; png-w3c-* and tiff6-predictor2-wrap-b* frame hand-derived raw bytes with independently weighted Adler sums.

rules.rule: Fields pack into low byte bits first, Huffman codes emit their high bit first; BFINAL ends the sequence, types 0/1/2 are stored/fixed/dynamic and type 3 is invalid; stored LEN/NLEN are complementary little-endian words after ignored alignment bits.
rules.implementation: Agrees with bit reading, canonical-code reversal, block dispatch and stored-block validation.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-stored-0/65535, flate-raw-stored-padding-*, fixed/dynamic vectors, flate-invalid-block-type and flate-invalid-bad-stored-length.

rules.rule: Length codes 257..285 describe 3..258 bytes and distance codes 0..29 describe 1..32768; references may overlap or cross blocks but cannot precede available history.
rules.implementation: Agrees with every base/extra-bit entry and bounded overlapping copies; the table assigns code 284 only 227..257, so extra=31 is rejected and 285 encodes 258.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-length-code-*, flate-all-distance-codes, flate-distance32768, flate-ring-wrap-overlap, flate-invalid-bad-distance and flate-invalid-length284-overflow.

rules.rule: Fixed literal lengths are 8/9/7/8 for ranges 0..143/144..255/256..279/280..287; all distance codes have five bits, but literal 286/287 and distance 30/31 cannot occur as data.
rules.implementation: Agrees with the fixed tables and reserved-code rejection.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-rfc1951-fixed-literal-boundaries, length-code vectors, flate-invalid-reserved-literal and flate-invalid-reserved-distance.

rules.rule: Dynamic headers describe 257..286 literal and 1..32 distance lengths; code-length symbols 0..18 use the prescribed permutation, with repeat 16 copying a preceding length and 17/18 repeating zero, including across the alphabet boundary.
rules.implementation: Agrees: 15-bit data-code and 7-bit length-code bounds, canonical assignment, required EOB and bounded repeat expansion are enforced.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-dynamic-length15, flate-rfc1951-repeat16-across-alphabets, flate-rfc1951-repeat17-zero, and invalid repeat-without-previous/repeat-overflow/missing-eob.

rules.rule: A code assignment must remain a prefix code with canonical ordering; oversubscribed lengths cannot assign distinct prefix codes.
rules.implementation: Agrees: rejects oversubscription in all three alphabets before constructing lookup tables.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-invalid-oversubscribed, flate-invalid-literal-oversubscribed and flate-invalid-distance-oversubscribed.

rules.rule: A single used distance code occupies one bit with an unused branch; one zero-length distance entry denotes an all-literal block.
rules.implementation: Agrees: the single-code tree decodes its used branch, and using an empty distance alphabet is an error.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-rfc1951-single-distance, flate-dynamic-single-empty-distance and flate-invalid-empty-distance-used.

rules.rule: The RFC explicitly describes the single-distance exception but gives no general complete-tree validity test for other incomplete canonical prefix codes.
rules.implementation: Documented decoder choice: reject other incomplete trees; accept a one-bit EOB-only literal tree and zero-only unused distance alphabets. These choices are not claimed as RFC-mandated acceptance/rejection.
rules.fixtures: Pins policy: flate-invalid-incomplete, flate-invalid-literal-incomplete, flate-invalid-distance-incomplete and flate-dynamic-single-empty-distance.

requirements.gaps: Colors>255 and Columns>u32::MAX exceed the public predictor fields and return Unsupported(predictor.dimensions). General incomplete-tree validity is unspecified in the supplied RFC and is documented as policy, not a pending primary-text review.
documented_choices: A valid zlib header wins detection; explicitly raw containers use decode_raw_deflate for header collisions. Bytes not recognized as CM=8 enter the reported raw path; Strict rejects that deviation.

General incomplete-tree rejection, the one-bit EOB-only literal exception and acceptance of zero-only unused distance alphabets are decoder choices where RFC 1951 does not explicitly settle validity; they are not verified normative prohibitions or permissions.
RFC 1951 3.1.1 determines wire packing for non-Huffman extra fields; 3.2.5 describes their integer values in conventional most-significant-bit notation.

rules.rule: LZW starts with clear=256, represents byte literals with 0..255, and ends with code 257.
rules.implementation: Agrees: initial clear is required, clears reset the dictionary and width, and EOD ends decoding.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: empty, special-phrase, reset and literal-only boundary vectors.

rules.rule: Codes are MSB-first, grow from 9 to at most 12 bits, and EarlyChange=1 advances each width transition by one code relative to 0.
rules.implementation: Agrees for both EarlyChange values; default is 1.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: lzw-iso-ec*-literal-boundary-* independently packs literal ordinals around width transitions.

rules.rule: A full encoder dictionary must be cleared before encoding more data.
rules.implementation: Strict rejects continued full-table data with filter.lzw-full-table; Repair freezes the full dictionary until clear/EOD and reports once per stream.
rules.fixtures: Conforming lzw-iso-ec*-full-clear has no diagnostic; missing-full-clear and frozen-table cases assert tagged Strict rejection and exact independently generated Repair output. frozen-entry4095-clear covers stable entries and a second full episode after clear with one diagnostic.

rules.rule: Unused bits in the EOD byte are zero.
rules.implementation: Strict rejects nonzero residual bits with filter.lzw-padding; Repair ignores those bits and reports the fault.
rules.fixtures: lzw-eod-nonzero-padding and lzw-eod-nonzero-padding-literal assert tagged Strict rejection and exact Repair output; valid streams retain zero padding.

rules.rule: Null decode parameters use defaults, including EarlyChange=1.
rules.implementation: Agrees after fixing null EarlyChange and predictor values.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: lzw-null-predictor-parameters.

rules.locator: TIFF 6.0 13, The Algorithm, pp.58-61; LZW Decoding, pp.61-62; ISO 32000-2 7.4.4.2
rules.rule: TIFF and PDF LZW share byte literals, clear=256, EOD=257 and MSB-first 9..12-bit codes; TIFF compressed byte order is independent of the TIFF II/MM word order.
rules.implementation: Agrees: codes pack high bit first across byte boundaries; no TIFF word-order switch belongs in the PDF decoder.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: lzw-ec1-empty/special and lzw-iso-ec1-literal-boundary-* independently pack MSB-first codes.

rules.rule: TIFF advances encoder widths after entries 511/1023/2047 and decoder widths after 510/1022/2046; this matches PDF EarlyChange=1, while PDF EarlyChange=0 delays each transition once.
rules.implementation: Agrees: default EarlyChange=1 is TIFF-compatible at width transitions; explicit 0 implements the PDF alternative, not a TIFF6 alternate mode.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: lzw-iso-ec{0,1}-literal-boundary-{254,255,766,767,1790,1791}, plus widths-reset and early-reset.

requirements.gaps: TIFF strip boundaries, FillOrder metadata and TIFF container byte order are outside this PDF decoder. Positive dimensions beyond the public predictor fields remain unsupported.
documented_choices: filter.lzw-full-table: ISO 7.4.4.2 requires an encoder clear when full. Strict rejects with this repair tag; Repair completes the decoder-lag entry and freezes codes through 4095, without subsequent insertion until clear/EOD. It records the repair once per stream, including across later clear codes. This recovery is project policy, not ISO permission.

filter.lzw-padding: ISO 7.4.4.2 requires zero unused EOD bits. Strict rejects with this repair tag; Repair ignores nonzero residual bits and records the deviation. This recovery is project policy, not ISO permission.

filter.corrupt: data no decoder accepts (an invalid DEFLATE block, code table, symbol or distance, an invalid LZW code, an invalid ASCIIHex or ASCII85 digit, z or end marker, an invalid PNG predictor tag) or an incomplete final predictor row ends the output: the whole rows decoded before it are kept and the repair is reported at the input offset. Strict keeps the decoder's error with this tag. zlib header errors, parameter errors, a one-digit or overflowing final ASCII85 group and budget errors stay errors. Images show the kept rows and leave the rest transparent. This recovery is project policy (owner decision 2026-10-27), not ISO permission.

rules.locator: 7.4.3, conversion equation and final partial-group paragraphs
rules.rule: Four bytes map to five base-85 digits; a partial binary group is zero-filled during encoding and emits only n+1 digits.
rules.implementation: Agrees, including maximum byte values and final groups of two to four digits.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: a85-partial-* and a85-iso-max-partial-1 through -4 derive the conversion independently.

rules.rule: Out-of-range full groups, z inside a group, and one-digit final groups are invalid.
rules.implementation: Agrees: all three are Syntax errors.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: a85-invalid-* covers overflow, misplaced z and a one-digit tail.

rules.rule: ASCII85 ignores PDF whitespace and uses z for a full zero group and the ~> marker to terminate.
rules.implementation: Agrees after fixing whitespace handling between the EOD marker characters, consistent with the clause-wide whitespace rule.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: a85-z-whitespace, a85-eod-whitespace and truncated/trailing cases.

documented_choices: Five zero digits are accepted for a zero group although the clause describes encoding that group as z; acceptance of that noncanonical spelling is a documented decoder choice.

rules.rule: Pairs of case-insensitive hexadecimal digits produce bytes, whitespace is ignored, > ends data, and an odd last digit has a low zero nibble.
rules.implementation: Agrees: invalid non-hex input is Syntax; missing termination is a reported repair.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: hex-binascii, hex-odd-whitespace, hex-invalid and hex-missing-end.

rules.rule: Tags 0..127 copy the next tag+1 bytes, tags 129..255 repeat one byte 257-tag times, and 128 ends the stream.
rules.implementation: Agrees with all packet branches and bounds; truncation goes through reported repair.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: run-literals, run-repeats, run-truncated and run-repeat-truncated.

rules.rule: Predictor defaults to 1; prediction uses positive color counts, a row sample count, and component depths 1/2/4/8/16.
rules.implementation: Agrees for representable dimensions; overlarge positive fields explicitly return Unsupported.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: PNG grid spans all component depths and color counts 1/3/5/255.

rules.rule: All Predictor values 10..15 select PNG decoding, with the incoming row tag choosing the algorithm even when the parameter differs from the encoder selection.
rules.implementation: Agrees: no fixed-tag enforcement is required for values 10..14.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: png-iso-row-tag-predictor-10 through -15 each use Up-tagged rows.

rules.rule: Rows are byte-rounded and high-bit-first, PNG prediction acts on bytes, and out-of-image neighbors are zero.
rules.implementation: Agrees with row layout, byte-wise reversal and boundary handling.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: packed/16-bit grids and predictor-png-distance-beyond-cap.

rules.rule: Each nonempty row has a tag 0..4; reconstruction is byte-wise identity, left, above, Average or Paeth addition modulo 256, with missing neighbors zero.
rules.implementation: Agrees with tags, byte stride and row boundaries; PDF supplies the permitted component/color layout instead of PNG container restrictions.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: predictor-b*-c*-n*-p1 and png-iso-row-tag-predictor-10..15, including packed and 16-bit samples.

rules.rule: Average adds the floor of the mean of left and above, computing their sum without eight-bit overflow.
rules.implementation: Agrees: the equivalent bitwise average rounds down without overflowing.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: png-w3c-average-overflow uses an odd sum of 509 and reconstructs a modular wrap.

rules.rule: Paeth computes exact signed distances from left+above-corner, selecting the nearest neighbor with ties preferring left, then above, then corner.
rules.implementation: Agrees: signed 16-bit arithmetic covers all byte values and the comparison order preserves ties.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: png-w3c-paeth-tie-left, png-w3c-paeth-tie-above and png-w3c-paeth-wide-sum.

requirements.gaps: Colors>255 and Columns>u32::MAX exceed the current public fields. This verifies the PDF predictor subset, not PNG containers, interlacing or chunk validation.
documented_choices: A partial row or a lone final tag is rejected rather than synthesizing samples.
Unused final-byte padding bits are preserved; no claim is made that the external predictor text requires this policy.
Supplied dimension fields are validated even with Predictor=1; ISO does not separately prescribe that validation policy.
Columns<=0 is rejected to ensure a nonempty row; Table 8 gives a row sample count but no separate explicit numeric minimum.

rules.locator: 7.4.4.4, TIFF paragraph and final group-difference bullet
rules.rule: Predictor=2 uses the prior component of the same color to the left, accounting for component depth and components per sample, with no row tag.
rules.implementation: Agrees with interleaved sample-wise reversal for 1/2/4/8/16 bits.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: TIFF grid, tiff-padding-preserved and predictor-tiff-ring-wrap.

rules.rule: Rows are whole-byte, high-bit-first sequences and components outside the image are zero.
rules.implementation: Agrees with checked layout, packing and left boundary handling.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: odd-width packed grids and independent sample encoding.

rules.locator: TIFF 6.0 14, Predictor and The algorithm, pp.64-65; ISO 32000-2 7.4.4.3, Table 8
rules.rule: Predictor tag 317 defaults to 1 and value 2 denotes horizontal differencing of whole components, discarding subtraction overflow at the component depth.
rules.implementation: Agrees: inversion adds the previous same-color component modulo 2^BitsPerComponent for PDF depths 1/2/4/8/16; packed components are unpacked logically and 16-bit carry is component-wise.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: tiff6-predictor2-wrap-b{1,2,4,8,16} and the TIFF predictor grids verify every PDF depth.

rules.rule: Horizontal differencing resets each row and interleaved colors use a SamplesPerPixel component stride; PDF specifies high-bit-first, byte-rounded packing.
rules.implementation: Agrees: first-pixel components are unchanged, preceding rows do not contribute, and 16-bit PDF components use high byte first irrespective of TIFF file word order.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: tiff6-predictor2-wrap-b* uses two colors and two rows; odd-width grids and tiff-padding-preserved pin packing and the padding policy.

requirements.gaps: Colors>255 and Columns>u32::MAX exceed the public fields. This verifies the PDF Predictor 2 arithmetic, not TIFF containers or other TIFF sample layouts.
documented_choices: Unused row padding bits are preserved and partial rows rejected; these policies are not asserted as external-TIFF-verified.
Columns<=0 is rejected to ensure a nonempty row; Table 8 gives a row sample count but no separate explicit numeric minimum.

rules.locator: CONTRIBUTING.md, Principles and Rust quality bar
rules.rule: Decoded buffers enforce the caller cap before growth or expansion; untrusted declarations do not authorize larger output.
rules.implementation: Agrees; this is project resource policy, not an ISO-prescribed numeric limit.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: flate-bomb and cap-minus-one checks on every nonempty valid or repaired vector.

documented_choices: The same cap applies to each filter-chain intermediate; PNG row tags do not count as final decoded bytes.

rules.rule: Deviations such as missing end markers are errors in Strict and may yield a documented prefix only through the diagnostic sink in Repair.
rules.implementation: Agrees with the project recovery contract, including tagged Strict errors and once-per-stream full-table diagnostics; ISO does not mandate these recovery choices.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: every repaired vector checks Strict rejection, exact Repair bytes and diagnostic identity.

documented_choices: Truncated prefixes are retained; checksum mismatches may retain decoded data; trailing bytes are ignored with a diagnostic except accepted ASCII whitespace; raw Flate data uses a diagnostic.
EOF acceptance, checksum recovery, trailing-byte handling and raw fallback are project recovery choices, not verified standard permissions.

Strict rejects with this repair tag; Repair completes the decoder-lag entry and freezes codes through 4095, without subsequent insertion until clear/EOD. It records the repair once per stream, including across later clear codes. This recovery is project policy, not ISO permission.

filter.lzw-padding: ISO 7.4.4.2 requires zero unused EOD bits. Strict rejects with this repair tag; Repair ignores nonzero residual bits and records the deviation. This recovery is project policy, not ISO permission.

rules.implementation: Agrees with ordered construction and decoding.
rules.fixtures: Agrees: filter-chain-iso-order and chains_pair_filters_with_parameters_and_borrow_plain_data.

documented_choices: Inline-image filter aliases are recognized by the shared name API; validating their enclosing syntax is outside this requirement.

rules.rule: Emit a zlib header without FDICT, a complete DEFLATE block sequence and big-endian Adler-32; stored blocks align and complement LEN, and compressed blocks obey the fixed/dynamic alphabets and match ranges.
rules.implementation: Agrees: all three block types, exact bit-cost selection, cross-block history and deterministic Fast/Default modes.
rules.fixtures: compress-empty/tiny/incompressible/dynamic select all three types; every codec input and expected output round-trips at both levels and is independently inflated by Python zlib.

rules.rule: Canonical literal/distance codes have at most 15 bits; code-length codes have at most 7 bits and use the prescribed order and repeat symbols.
rules.implementation: Agrees: binary package-merge constructs complete bounded trees with stable ties.
rules.fixtures: Exhaustive small optimal-cost oracle and skewed Huffman tests, plus Python validation of dynamic output.

rules.rule: Bound input, output and encoder work before growth; no global state or host capabilities enter compression.
rules.implementation: Input uses decoded_bytes; output uses stream_bytes; matcher visits at most 32/128 links and 258 bytes per match, and scratch is bounded by one 65535-byte block plus 32 KiB window and finite Huffman alphabets.
rules.fixtures: Exact input/output budget tests and multiblock/window-wrap/lazy fixtures.

documented_choices: Fast is greedy with at most 32 chain links; Default uses 128 links and one-byte lazy matching. These are effort choices, not zlib numerical level compatibility.

Block boundaries are at 65535 input bytes. Selection compares exact encoded bit costs of the generated token sequence, including dynamic headers, stored alignment and final padding; equal costs prefer fixed, then stored. This is not global parsing/block-boundary optimality.
Package-merge is an independent construction algorithm; the RFC prescribes code properties, not a tree-building method.

Huffman package storage scales with the active alphabet, including at most two dummy symbols; matching compares bounded chunks and rejects candidates unable to improve the current length. These choices preserve the encoded token sequence while reducing temporary allocation and prefix comparisons.

rules.rule: PNG starts with its signature and IHDR, has consecutive zlib IDAT data, and ends with IEND; each chunk CRC covers its type and data, excluding its length.
rules.implementation: Agrees: non-interlaced eight-bit Gray/RGB/RGBA, positive 31-bit dimensions, 64 KiB IDAT payloads and reflected CRC-32.
rules.fixtures: Python independently parses every chunk, checks binascii CRCs, headers and complete zlib termination; png-encode-rgba-multiple-idat covers chunk splitting.

rules.rule: Apply one of five byte filters per row; the recommended adaptive heuristic minimizes absolute signed filtered bytes.
rules.implementation: Agrees: all five candidates are scored with wide arithmetic; ties prefer the lower tag.
rules.fixtures: png-encode-{gray,rgb,rgba}-filter{0..4}; Python independently unfilters pixels and recomputes the adaptive minimum.

rules.rule: RGBA stores RGB followed by unassociated alpha; transparent and partially transparent colors remain sample data.
rules.implementation: Agrees: input straight alpha and hidden colors are copied without conversion.
rules.fixtures: png-encode-straight-alpha, rgba-one-pixel and independent exact-pixel comparison.

rules.rule: Check pixel and byte budgets, dimensions and the exact input byte count before encoding.
rules.implementation: Agrees: pixels and decoded_bytes bound input, stream_bytes bounds complete PNG including framing; a filtered-image buffer adds one bounded tag per row. Invalid dimensions and pixel counts return InvalidArgument; budgets/overflow/allocation return Limit, all positioned.
rules.fixtures: Dimension, short/long pixel slice, overflow and exact output cap tests.

requirements.gaps: Only eight-bit Gray/RGB/straight RGBA, non-interlaced; no palette, ancillary colour metadata or streaming encoder API.
documented_choices: Adaptive filter ties choose the lower numeric tag. IDAT payloads are at most 65536 bytes.
PNG has no implicit colour-space conversion or unpremultiplication; callers provide straight samples and their colour-management policy.
Scratch includes one filtered image plus two rows and bounded compression state. Filter tags are additional framing beyond the decoded pixel byte budget.
